8.en: Though any mission begins with a set Subtlety rating, the party’s choices and activities during the mission cause it to increase or decrease. Enough change can eventually push Subtlety to a new level, typically deteriorating, changing the narrative and mechanical impacts on the further mission. At the end of an encounter and whenever the party engages in relevant activities between encounters, the GM should consider the events since the last Subtlety adjustment and increase or decrease accordingly. The questions in the @UUID[.XyTxLhjDZDkpE0Lz#changing-subtlety-ratings]{Changing Subtlety Ratings} Table are a great primer for judging what can trigger Subtlety changes, but they don’t cover every possibility.

16.en: But there are always opportunities for parties to throw caution to the wind and do something dramatic to make their Subtlety Ratings plummet. Conversely, the GM may even have a plot twist up their sleeve to do the same (after all, no one is stopping an Inquisition Patron from announcing their acolyte’s existence). In such cases, the GM should choose a Level and shift their party’s rating to the best fit.

20.en: Changing circumstances within the party’s area of operation may also cause Subtlety adjustments. For example, if the party is operating in a hive and the Governor orders a hive-spanning security lockdown, the party’s Subtlety could naturally decrease since there are more eyes on the people. On the other hand, if the local populace is suddenly affected by a breakout daemonic plague, the presence of Inquisitorial entities may not be the people’s greatest priority, allowing the party’s Subtlety to increase.
